hypothesis: Replacing the saturating product-form cut probability with a fan-out-normalised star (pairwise) expansion sum over pins of (p_i - mean_p_net)^2 / (k-1) keeps a usable gradient on large/high-fan-out nets (clock, reset) so the partition actually decides those nets instead of leaving them saturated, reducing TNS via fewer badly-cut hub nets.
analysis: Hypothesis failed: all circuits worsened (total −0.867), with C3 worst (dWNS −86%, dTNS −28%). Cut nets, weighted cut, and critical-pair cross-tier crossings all rose (C3 crit_cross 0.069→0.296), and repair flips barely changed—so the fan-out-normalised star did not rescue hub nets; it increased crossings and criticality. Seed spread is high (std 0.125; C2 per-seed −0.05 to −0.50), indicating instability. Next step: gate the star term by fan-out (only apply above a threshold) or blend it with the product form, and re-test on C3 with more seeds.
